title: Heavy lifting
blurb: A cart sunk to its axles in a mire, a stubborn carter, and whatever is lying about the lane.
after: Many ways shift a heavy thing. Hands help: people who are willing count. The world decides what really works.
refines: Does the judge accept a sound way and refuse a weak one? Do players find people as aids (will_help)?
goal: Get Wat's cart out of the mire

things.name: the mire
things.description: Deep, sticky black mud across the lane. The cart's wheels are sunk in it to the axles.

things.name: loaded cart
things.description: Wat's heavy two-wheeled cart, sunk to the axles in the mire, with four barrels of cider roped aboard.

things.name: barrels of cider
things.description: Four full barrels of cider roped on the cart: a quarter of a ton between them.

things.name: Bess the ox
things.description: Bess, Wat's big brown ox, still yoked and unhitched from the cart, chewing patiently. She can pull a great weight if she's led.

things.name: stout rope
things.description: A stout hemp rope, ten yards of it.

things.name: loose fence rail
things.description: A long, stout split-oak fence rail, hanging loose from the fence: nobody's mended it in years.

things.name: big flat stone
things.description: A big flat stone by the boulder: heavy, but one person could roll it.

things.name: old boards
things.description: A pile of old planks, grey and sound.

things.name: round logs
things.description: Round barked logs, each as thick as a leg: they'd roll.

steps.title: Sedge Bottom
cards: …signal. A lane with a cart sunk to its axles in a mire, four barrels of cider aboard. Wat the carter has pushed till he's blue.

There are many ways to shift a heavy thing: levers, boards, rollers, a beast, a rope, lightening the load, or more hands. People who are willing to help count. The world decides if your way really works.
There's no one right way, and no words to copy. The device helps if you ask (H).

steps.title: Out of the mire
cards: Get Wat's cart out of the mire.

on_done.text: She's out! Ha! Friend, you've saved my neck. If you're ever at the Ford Inn, the cider's on me.

on_done.lead: Wat says the cider's on him at the Ford Inn.
on_done.said: The cider's on me at the Ford Inn.

steps.done: Out. How you did it was yours; whether it worked was the world's.
help: Look at what's lying about ({right-click}): a long rail, a big flat stone, boards, logs, the ox, Wat's rope.
Or ask for hands: talk to Wat, Dunna and Rook. Those in the conversation with you will heave if you ask.

playtest.do: push the long fence rail under the cart's axle over the big flat stone as a fulcrum, lever the wheels up out of the mud, and shove the old boards under them, then roll the cart forward onto the boards

2.say: We'll never do it alone. Dunna, Rook, will you lend a hand? All of us at once.
Dunna, will you push with us on three?

2.do: with Wat, Dunna and Rook all heaving at the wheels and the tailboard together on three, rock the cart and push it up out of the mire

try_also: lever the cart out of the mud with the fence rail on the flat stone, and put boards under the wheels

reactions.killed: …You killed someone. That can't be undone. Rewind from the menu if that isn't what you meant.
reactions.arrested: They've taken you away. Rewind from the menu to try again.
reactions.dead: You died. Rewind to the last calm moment and try something else.
